subject: G-03 — deriveState.ts returns service_ok ahead of every check, overriding a detector that fired
question: SUTRADHARA/M0-T24: deriveState.ts:65 returns 'service_ok' as the FIRST statement for any service asset, and plan.ts:196 READY_STATES makes that green dependency-satisfying. ka_graha_sancara ran its own self-test on 2026-08-02, wrote service_health='unhealthy', and still renders green. ruling: CONFIRMED BY MY OWN INSPECTION AND GRANTED AS TRACK M, SPLIT INTO WHAT IS FORCED NOW AND WHAT IS M3's. I read the code rather than accept the report: deriveState.ts:65 is 'if (asset.asset_type === service || asset.asset_kind === service) return service_ok' and it IS the first statement — ahead of is_active, ahead of incomplete, ahead of error, ahead of actualRows. It is worse than reported in one respect nobody named: because it precedes the is_active check, an INACTIVE service also renders service_ok. plan.ts:196 READY_STATES = {lit, service_ok} and :250 treats a dep in that set as satisfied, so a service whose own detector said 'unhealthy' satisfies downstream build prerequisites. The function's comment states the claim it cannot support — 'they are healthy when registered + CURRENT' — while checking neither CURRENT nor anything else; four of the eight affected assets are not CURRENT. This is H4 in its purest form: not a green with no detector, but A GREEN OVERRIDING A DETECTOR THAT ALREADY RAN AND RETURNED THE OPPOSITE ANSWER. That is worse than every instance this campaign has catalogued so far, because in the others no one had looked; here someone looked, wrote down 'unhealthy', and the serving layer discarded it. (1) SCOPE: THIS IS TRACK M AND DOES NOT WAIT FOR A RUNG — and SUTRADHARA's reasoning for distinguishing it from the ka_kshetra string (PARK-5) is correct and I adopt it as the test. For PARK-5 the two scope tests CONFLICT: §8.2's bright-line ('does it change rows in an asset's target table') says Track M, while Track M's definition ('layer-independent machinery') says no, because that string is about one asset and repairing it well needs R3's understanding. That conflict is why PARK-5 is parked. HERE BOTH TESTS AGREE: deriveState is generic code governing every service asset in every layer (R0's two, R3's three, R5's two), no single rung owns it, it changes no asset's rows, and repairing it needs no asset-specific knowledge whatsoever — it needs the function to consult the detector instead of a declared string. Where both tests agree there is no invariant exception to make, so no P7 arises and PARK-5's parking is not weakened by this grant. If it waited for a rung it would wait for R5, and until then a service_ok outranking an 'unhealthy' reading keeps satisfying dependencies. (2) FORCED NOW, AND NOT OPTIONAL: deriveState MUST NOT RETURN service_ok WHEN A REAL DETECTOR VERDICT EXISTS AND SAYS OTHERWISE. ka_graha_sancara's stored 'unhealthy' must win over the declared type/kind. This requires no design judgement and closes the H4. The early return must also stop preceding the is_active check. (3) DEFERRED TO M3, DELIBERATELY: what a service with NO probe should render, and whether that state belongs in READY_STATES. Five of the eight have a NULL health_probe, so there is no verdict to consult, and the honest answer is 'unknown' rather than either green or red — but choosing that vocabulary and deciding whether unknown satisfies a dependency is exactly the integrity-gate engine's territory, which §14.1 assigns to M3 ('writes lit only on pass'). IF ANY CURRENTLY-DISPATCHABLE BUILD WOULD BE BLOCKED, RETURN TO ME BEFORE WRITING. An asset that stops satisfying a dependency was never entitled to satisfy it — that is D-24's logic and it holds — but the blast radius must be measured, not discovered. No rung is open and no build is running, which makes this the safest possible moment. subject: Seed-vs-DB ownership of registry metadata — measured; D-19 refined into three classes
question: M0-T29 completed the durability register: 23 of 23 seed-overwritten columns modelled, 0 UNKNOWN, a re-seed moves 260 cells across 96 assets. Three exposures remain and the register states it has NO BASIS to decide which side is right for 80 cells of count_sql / target_floor / depends_on. That is D-19's question with a number attached. How is it settled, and at every rung?
ruling: D-19'S PRINCIPLE STANDS AND IS NOW REFINED INTO THREE CLASSES, BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT SHOWS TWO WERE NOT ENOUGH. First the reassuring half, which the register reported plainly rather than manufacturing risk to justify itself: MOST CAMPAIGN REPAIRS ARE DURABLE. domain, rung, superseded_by, data_disposition, has_substeps, has_writer, integrity_check_sql, clear_tables, service_health and writer_timeout_seconds appear in NEITHER of the seed's column lists. So D-19's alarm was correctly raised and is correctly narrowed by evidence — which is what measurement is for. (1) THE THIRD CLASS D-19 MISSED. I split registry fields into DECLARED (seed owns) and MEASURED (campaign owns, must leave the SET clause). The 80 cells prove a third exists, and it is why the register honestly reported no basis to choose: DECLARED-BUT-VERIFIABLE — a value that is legitimately authored in source AND checkable against reality. count_sql and depends_on are exactly this. A DAG edge SHOULD be declared in source, where it is reviewable and diffable, and SHOULD be audited against what the code actually reads (that is SQ-01's whole purpose); it should not live only in a database where no diff shows it changing. So neither surface is unconditionally right, and the register was correct to refuse to pick — the error would have been picking. (2) THE RULING, PER CLASS. (a) MEASURED — target_floor. Campaign owns it; it must leave the seed's DO UPDATE SET or be guarded MR-06-style. I7 sets a floor to the MEASURED ACHIEVED COUNT and a declarative file structurally cannot hold a measured value, so seed ownership of this column collides with I7 at EVERY rung, exactly as SUTRADHARA framed it. D-19 stands, now with a number behind it. (b) DECLARED-BUT-VERIFIABLE — count_sql, depends_on. They STAY in the seed as the declaration. What must change is that DIVERGENCE IS NEVER SILENTLY RESOLVED BY WHOEVER RUNS LAST: a seed run must produce a divergence report for these columns before writing, and the divergence is reconciled at the owning rung's Conform, on the merits, per cell. This is D-25's rule applied one layer over — declare in source, verify independently, SURFACE THE PAIR rather than let one side quietly win. (c) OPERATIONAL COROLLARY, FORCED BY THE EVIDENCE AND EASY TO MISS: a Conform repair to a declared-but-verifiable field MUST LAND IN BOTH SURFACES, or in the seed alone. Writing depends_on to the DB while the seed still declares the old value simply recreates the reversion this register was built to find. Every rung's Conform stage inherits this; it is not an M0 special case. (3) THE TWO OTHER EXPOSURES, BOTH FIXED IN M0. (a) asset_kind/asset_type: EIGHT rows, not six, because NOT ONE of the eight seed entries declares the key at all and assetKind/assetType DEFAULT TO 'data' when omitted (:3268). THE DEFAULT IS AN ACTIVE WRITE, NOT A NO-OP — modelling an absent column as 'unchanged' would have reported 0 and produced a falsely reassuring register. That trap is the single most valuable thing in this deliverable and I want it stated in the ledger, because 'absent means unchanged' is the intuition everyone brings and it is wrong here. Fix: declare BOTH keys explicitly in all eight entries so the default can never fire. (b) mi_jivanaghatana: live scope=per_chart/domain=chart, seed declares scope:'global'; scope is seed-overwritten and domain is not, so a re-seed moves ONE HALF OF A DERIVED PAIR and leaves the row internally inconsistent. This is a new sub-shape worth naming — not reversion but DESYNCHRONISATION OF A DERIVED PAIR — and any column pair where one half is seed-owned and the other campaign-owned has it latent. Fix the seed's declaration to match the measured truth; and check for other split pairs. (4) NOT WALL-CLOCK URGENT, AND I AM SAYING SO EXPLICITLY SO NOBODY RUSHES IT: the seeder still cannot complete a run because of the bg_cohort abort, so nothing can revert anything today. That is the same interlock D-19 identified holding a third hazard, and it reinforces rather than weakens D-19's ruling that bg_cohort must not be repaired until all of them are closed. STANDING REQUIREMENT for repairs of this class, with conditions: the drill runs inside an explicit transaction that is ALWAYS rolled back and never committed; post-checks re-run after the rollback; the execution is disclosed in the report.
